title: Adding support for ArduPilot
body:
## Context

A while ago, @peterbarker worked on adding support for APM in the SDK ([here](https://github.com/peterbarker/DroneCore/tree/ardupilot)). More recently, @jinchengde (and others) started looking into that, again. The goal of this issue is to discuss the high-level requirements and architecture.

## Benefits for APM

The project is architectured in such a way that everything relies on a C++ MAVLink implementation. Making this implementation compatible with APM means that APM will also get the language bindings ([Python](https://github.com/dronecode/dronecodesdk-python), [Swift](https://github.com/dronecode/dronecodesdk-swift), [Java](https://github.com/dronecore/dronecore-java) and future ones like [Javascript](https://github.com/mrpollo/DronecodeSDK-JavaScript)).

The interface common to all our bindings is defined [here](https://github.com/Dronecode/DronecodeSDK-Proto/tree/master/protos) and is used to auto-generate language-specific APIs (e.g. using RxSwift in Swift, RxJava in Java, and asyncio in Python).

## SDK architecture (overview)

The SDK can been seen as composed from 4 parts:

1. The [interface definition](https://github.com/Dronecode/DronecodeSDK-Proto/tree/master/protos) (protobuf files), common to all the languages (C++, Swift, Java, Python). Each proto file is considered a "plugin", which is a group of (MAVLink) features.
2. The C++ [MAVLink implementation](https://github.com/Dronecode/DronecodeSDK), which actually maintains a connection to the drone and does the MAVLink logic.
3. The [backend](https://github.com/Dronecode/DronecodeSDK/tree/develop/backend), which exposes the C++ implementation of (2) as a messaging server through the interface of (1).
4. The language bindings ([Python](https://github.com/dronecode/dronecodesdk-python), [Swift](https://github.com/dronecode/dronecodesdk-swift), [Java](https://github.com/dronecore/dronecore-java)), which implement (1) to communicate with the backend (3).

At the lowest level, each plugin (defined by one proto file) is a C++ library. The backend uses those libraries, as can been seen [here](https://github.com/Dronecode/DronecodeSDK/blob/develop/backend/src/CMakeLists.txt#L38-L46).

title: mavlink_direct: Message filtering not working in subscribe_message (v3.10.1)
body:
## Bug Description
The `mavlink_direct` plugin's `subscribe_message` method does not properly filter messages when a specific `message_name` is provided. Instead of receiving only the requested message type, subscribers receive ALL message types.

## Expected Behavior
When subscribing with a specific message name (e.g., `message_name="HEARTBEAT"`), the subscriber should only receive messages of that type.

## Actual Behavior
Subscribers receive ALL message types regardless of the filter specified. The `message_name` parameter is completely ignored.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Start MAVSDK server v3.10.1
2. Connect via gRPC and use the mavlink_direct service
3. Call `SubscribeMessage` with `message_name="HEARTBEAT"`
4. Observe that you receive all message types (ATTITUDE, TIMESYNC, GPS_RAW_INT, etc.)

## Test Results
Testing with a Python gRPC client shows:
- **No filter (empty string)**: Correctly receives all 34 message types
- **Filter "HEARTBEAT"**: Incorrectly receives all 34 message types (should only receive HEARTBEAT)
- **Filter "TIMESYNC"**: Incorrectly receives all 34 message types (should only receive TIMESYNC)
- **Filter "ATTITUDE"**: Incorrectly receives all 34 message types (should only receive ATTITUDE)

## Root Cause Analysis
Looking at the code in `mavlink_direct_impl.cpp`:
- The `subscribe_message` method stores the `message_name` filter
- It registers with `SystemImpl::register_libmav_message_handler`
- However, when messages arrive, they're forwarded to ALL subscribers regardless of their individual filters
- The stored `message_name` is never actually used to filter messages before invoking callbacks

## Environment
- MAVSDK version: v3.10.1
- OS: Ubuntu 22.04
- Connection: gRPC on port 50051
- Test vehicle: PX4 SITL

## Workaround
Until fixed, users must manually filter messages in their client code:
```python
# Subscribe to all messages (empty filter)
request = mavlink_direct_pb2.SubscribeMessageRequest(message_name="")
responses = stub.SubscribeMessage(request)

for response in responses:
    if response.HasField('message'):
        msg = response.message
        # Manual filtering
        if msg.message_name == "HEARTBEAT":
            # Process only HEARTBEAT messages
            process_message(msg)
```

## Impact
This bug makes the filtering feature completely non-functional, forcing all clients to receive and process all messages, which can significantly impact performance in high-frequency telemetry scenarios.

title: mavsdk.pc forces bundled private dependencies on shared-library consumers
body:
### Problem

The generated `mavsdk.pc` declares implementation dependencies as pkg-config private requirements:

```pkgconfig
Requires.private: libcurl jsoncpp tinyxml2
```

(Current `main` uses `nlohmann_json` instead of `jsoncpp`, but retains the same structure.)

For the prebuilt shared-library packages, these dependencies are bundled into `libmavsdk.so`. They are not exposed through MAVSDK's installed public headers and are not dynamic dependencies of the installed shared object. Nevertheless, pkg-config attempts to resolve the private modules when compiler flags are requested.

On a clean Debian 13 ARM64 system with MAVSDK 3.17.2 installed:

```console
$ pkg-config --modversion mavsdk
3.17.2

$ pkg-config --libs mavsdk
-lmavsdk

$ pkg-config --cflags mavsdk
Package libcurl was not found in the pkg-config search path.
Package 'libcurl', required by 'mavsdk', not found
Package 'jsoncpp', required by 'mavsdk', not found
Package 'tinyxml2', required by 'mavsdk', not found
```

This prevents the conventional command from working:

```sh
c++ example.cpp $(pkg-config --cflags --libs mavsdk)
```

CMake consumers using `find_package(MAVSDK)` build and run successfully on the same system.

### Package inspection

I reproduced this while producing and testing a Debian 13 ARM64 build from the v3.17.2 tag, and also confirmed that the official v3.17.2 Debian 13 AMD64 package contains the same `Requires.private` line.

For the ARM64 shared object:

```console
$ readelf -d /usr/lib/libmavsdk.so.3.17.2 | grep NEEDED
Shared library: [libstdc++.so.6]
Shared library: [libm.so.6]
Shared library: [libgcc_s.so.1]
Shared library: [libc.so.6]
```

The installed MAVSDK public headers do not include curl, jsoncpp, or tinyxml2 headers. The package supplies the shared library and no static `libmavsdk.a`.

### Expected behavior

Installing the shared-library development package should be sufficient for:

```sh
pkg-config --cflags --libs mavsdk
```

Private implementation dependencies already incorporated into `libmavsdk.so` should not require their development packages on the consumer system.

### Suggested fix

Remove `Requires.private` from `mavsdk.pc` for shared-library builds/packages, or generate it conditionally only for a static installation whose final consumer genuinely needs those external archives.

This is related to #2475, which covers the separate hard-coded CI-prefix problem in the generated pkg-config file.

My concern is that it adds complexity to the CMake setup. The goal of making the superbuild optional was that instead of supporting all possible use-cases, we would let advanced users handle dependencies themselves.

Ideally, MAVSDK upstream would not maintain distro packages. In my opinion it is the role of package maintainers to do that for their distro. It's impossible for MAVSDK upstream to properly maintain packages for all distros. In this case, I feel like the reason you need this mix between system libraries and vendored libraries is that mavlink, libevent, picosha2 and libmavlike are not `.deb` packages themselves (and mavlink especially is fundamentally difficult to standardise as a `.deb`, which complicates matters). On the other hand, we need a superbuild because most users don't know how to [handle dependencies themselves](https://www.acarg.ch/posts/cmake-deps/) 🤷.
